title: Teaching Some Python to Your Spreadsheets
text:
What is grist?


Grist is a modern relational spreadsheet. It combines the flexibility of a spreadsheet with the robustness of a database.
It can run:

locally (docker or desktop)
in the cloud or homelab
like Google Docs at https://getgrist.com





It stores everything as a SQLite database that is easy to share and backup



Talk about the SMVE (check if time allows)

section: A CLI client for the API
text:
A CLI client for the API
pygrister is a Python library and a CLI for grist.
It requires an URL and an API key, but more configuration can be passed.
This in example .env we could use in our workshop repo:
GRIST_API_KEY=22...36
GRIST_SELF_MANAGED=Y
GRIST_SELF_MANAGED_HOME=http://localhost:8484
GRIST_SELF_MANAGED_SINGLE_ORG=N
GRIST_SERVER_PROTOCOL=http
GRIST_TEAM_SITE=docs

Service Accounts

It’s a bit dangerous to give full access to our documents to any automation with the user API key (GRIST_API_KEY)
Service Accounts are pseudo-users which can be given finer grained access to a a few tables
There’s not UI for creating service accounts, but gry CLI comes handy.

Marimo

Marimo is a modern Python notebook centered around the idea of reproducibility
The notebooks are not .ipynb format (JSON) but .py
A notebook can also be a script, a test suite and an application.
Takes advantage of modern python packaging like with uv for sandboxing.

title: Teaching Some Python to Your Spreadsheets
text:
Connecting through MCP

mcp-server-grist is a MCP server written in Python. It allows AI applications like Claude, IBM Bob, Codex, pi, OpenClaw, Hermes, etc. to connect to the Grist API.



This is not the official MCP that lives in https://<yoursite>.getgrist.com/mcp for the commercial version, so authentication will use the same API KEYs instead of OAauth2.



To run mcp-server-grist with uv we need these two environment variables:

GRIST_API_KEY (user or Service Account)
GRIST_API_URL (this will be where Grist is running + /api)
